title: Gravity
examples: Teacher, if I go to the Moon, will my weight change?
What is the difference between my mass and my weight?
Does gravity only pull things down?

explain.say: Gravity is a force that pulls things with mass towards each other. This pull is always present between any two objects.
The more mass an object has, the stronger its gravitational pull will be. Bigger things pull harder on smaller things.
Mass is how much 'stuff' an object has, measured in kilograms. It stays the same everywhere you go.
Weight is the pull of gravity on an object's mass. We measure weight using a scale in Newtons.
Because Earth has a lot of mass, it pulls everything towards its center. This keeps us firmly on the ground.
When you are on the Moon, gravity is weaker, so your weight changes. But your actual mass stays exactly the same.

faq.q: If mass stays the same, why does weight change on the Moon?
faq.a: Weight is a measure of the force of gravity pulling on your mass. Since the Moon has less mass than Earth, its gravitational pull is weaker.
asks: Why is my weight different on the Moon?

faq.q: Is weight the same thing as mass?
faq.a: No, they are different. Mass is the amount of matter you have, and weight is the measurement of the pull of gravity on that matter.
asks: What is the difference between mass and weight?
Do I have the same mass and weight everywhere?

faq.q: Does gravity pull things sideways too?
faq.a: Gravity pulls things towards the center of the large object creating it. On Earth, that center is right beneath our feet.
asks: Does gravity pull me left or right?

faq.q: What unit do we use to measure mass and weight?
faq.a: We measure mass in kilograms, which is a unit of matter. We measure weight in Newtons, which is a unit of force.
asks: Is mass measured in pounds or kilograms?
What is the unit for weight?

faq.q: Why do we not float away from Earth?
faq.a: Because Earth has a very large mass, it creates a strong gravitational pull. This force keeps everything connected to its center.
asks: What keeps us on the ground?
Is there a force holding us down?

facts: Gravity is a force of attraction between any two objects with mass.
Mass measures the amount of matter in an object, measured in kilograms.
Weight is the force of gravity acting on an object's mass, measured in Newtons.
The strength of gravity changes depending on the mass of the large body.

quiz.say: If you move from Earth to a planet with much less mass, what will happen to your weight?
quiz.why: Because the planet has less mass, its gravitational pull is weaker, making your weight less.

wrong.0: This is wrong because weight depends on the strength of the pull, which changes with the planet.
wrong.1: This is wrong because less mass means less pull, not more pull.
wrong.2: This is wrong because even small planets still have some gravitational pull.

quiz.say: Which measurement tells you how much 'stuff' an object contains?
quiz.why: Mass measures the actual amount of matter, like the number of atoms in an object.

wrong.1: Weight is a force measurement, not a measure of the amount of stuff.
wrong.2: Force is a general term; mass is the specific measurement of matter.
wrong.3: Pull is a description of the action, not the scientific measurement.

quiz.say: A student measures 40 kilograms on Earth and 40 kilograms on the Moon. Which measurement is correct for mass?
quiz.why: Mass is constant regardless of location because it measures the amount of matter.

wrong.1: Newtons measure weight (force), not the amount of matter.
wrong.2: This assumes the pull changes the amount of matter, which it does not.
wrong.3: This incorrectly assumes that being on the Moon somehow adds more matter.
